You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: On Penn RR (15). Next roll: 3 = Tenn $550 (2/36), 4 = NY $600 (3/36). $653 survives both ($103 / $53). Any build or cash trade makes NY a bankruptcy. Do not house browns yet — rents are weak vs that risk. p4 is also on 15 and moves before my next turn (p3 then p4), so they may scoop Kentucky/Indiana/Illinois/B&O first; nothing I can do. Save cash for reds ($220–240), B&O ($200), and later Pacific+NC to complete green with Penn Ave. Never sell Ventnor to p4. Do not fund p1 or p3.

Open at $1. Pacific makes me 2/3 green with Penn Ave; still need NC. p1 max $34, p3 max $100, p4 has $1703 and was just tipped to deny me. Cash $653; from RR a 4 is NY $600 (3/36) and a 3 is Tenn $550 (2/36). Can mortgage Med/Baltic/Ventnor/Penn ($30/$30/$80/$160) to cover, so not hard-capped at $53. Will go to about $150-180 if the price stays there. Above ~$200, drop and let p4 overpay for a denial chip. Do not trade Ventnor for Pacific alone. If p4 bids small, raise just over them next round.

Price out p3 ($100 max) and force p4 to pay real money or give me Pacific. $101 leaves $552; Tenn $550 is covered, NY $600 needs Med+Baltic mortgages ($60). Ceiling still ~$180–200 — above that drop and let p4 overpay for a denial chip. NC still unowned, so 2/3 green is worth contesting but not a war with $1703. Do not sell Ventnor.

Jump to $150, inside the $180–200 ceiling. p3 is out; p4 is matching to deny. $150 leaves $503 — still buys any red (Ky/Ind $220, Ill $240) or B&O, and a Tenn/NY hit is mortgage-survivable (Med+Baltic+Ventnor = $140). If p4 goes past ~$200, drop and let them overpay for a chip; NC is still unowned so 2/3 green is worth contesting but not a war with $1703. Reds remain the real win path. Do not sell Ventnor.

Drop. p4 is matching $1 over and has $1703; I will not win Pacific below their denial ceiling. I already own Penn Ave, so p4 cannot complete green without a trade I will not make. Pacific is only an offensive 2/3 chip that still needs NC, which they can also deny. Cash $653 is for orange survival (NY 3h ~$750 / Tenn 3h ~$700 need mortgages) and the unowned reds (Ky/Ind/Ill) plus B&O. Do not sell Ventnor. Contest NC only if the price is a true block, not a vanity set.

Buy at $240, cash $413. All 3 reds unowned; Illinois is the win path and list price caps what p4 can force. Auction just lets p4 deny or push me over $240. Orange rents stuck: p1 has $34 so no more houses. SJ 2h $200 covered; Tenn 3h $550 / NY 3h $600 need mortgages (capacity $350) but survivable. From pos 24 I cannot hit oranges this lap and may pass GO (+$200) first. Do not build browns. Contest Ky/Ind/B&O/NC. Never sell Ventnor or Penn Ave to p4.

Brown monopoly is the only set I can house. One house each costs $100 and leaves $313 — still buys a red ($220) or B&O ($200), and mortgage capacity (~$420) covers a dark-blue or orange hit. Unimproved brown rent is noise; even one house roughly triples it and starts a clock on p4 while they sit in jail. Even build required. Do not touch Ventnor or Penn Ave. Reds remain the real win path if I land on them.

Cash $313 is the reserve for reds (Ky/Ind $220), B&O ($200), and auction wars vs p4 ($1552). Another brown house pair costs $100 and drops me under red list price; 3-house build ($200) has better rent ROI but locks the only win path. Cannot hit reds/B&O/NC this roll (on Illinois). Do not sell houses. Never trade Ventnor (yellow mono for p4) or Penn Ave (green blocker). p1 on Pacific may pass GO (rolls 9-12) and rebuild oranges — cannot stop that. p3 may auction Virginia/Kentucky or die on oranges. End and contest those auctions.

Do not buy NC at $300. Cash $333→$33. Liquidation without NC ≈ $823 (cash $333 + sell 2 brown houses $50 + mortgages Med/Baltic/Ill/Ventnor/Penn $30+30+120+100+160), which covers current orange 3h (SJ $550 / Tenn $700 / NY $750). Buying adds only $150 mortgage value, net liquidation ≈ $673 — short of Tenn and NY. From space 32 a Chance/CC Go-to-Jail skips GO and puts me 6–9 from the oranges; dark-blue hits (PP $175 / BW $200 on rolls 5/7) also drain me before GO. p4 has $1652, owns Pacific, and will outbid me for 2/3 green — list price is the only cap, and it is too expensive. Auction, bid only if price stays ≤~$180–200 so post-buy liquidation still clears NY $750 (max bid ≈ $223 = 823+150−750). Above that, drop and let p4 pay. Never trade Ventnor (blocks their yellow) or Penn Ave. Reds (Ky/Ind still unowned) plus Illinois remain the win path; keep $333 to buy them. p1 may add a 4th orange house ($100) — even more reason to hoard cash.

Jump to $150, my walk-away. Mortgage value of NC is $150, so winning is liquidation-neutral vs passing ($823 either way) and flips green leverage: I hold 2/3 (NC+Penn), p4 stuck on Pacific. Cannot complete green anyway. Cash after buy $183 covers PP $175; BW $200 needs a small mortgage. I pass GO before any red, so +$200 restores a Kentucky/Indiana buy. If p4 bids $151+, drop — they have $1652 and will $1-increment forever. Do not trade Ventnor or Penn Ave. Reds remain the win path.
